summary: Backend validation of Spark Core 2.0 topic_tracker + disclaimer/intent_matcher blueprints. 4/7 tests pass. The original IndentationError in response_composer.py is structurally gone (file parses OK), but a NEW related bug remains: the topic_tracker integration is INCOMPLETE — compose_response references `topic` and `tt_cfg` at line 256 without ever defining them or calling detect_topic(). Every POST /api/spark/compose call now returns {success:false, error:"name 'tt_cfg' is not defined", fallback:true}. Disclaimer blueprint, intent_matcher routing, blueprint reload, and topic_tracker config in blueprint all work correctly.

critical.issue: compose_response() in /app/backend/modules/chat/response_composer.py references `topic` (line 256) and `tt_cfg` (line 256) in its return dict, but neither variable is defined in the function scope. `tt_cfg` is only defined locally inside `_build_system_prompt`. The function also never calls `detect_topic()` from topic_tracker.py, so the topic_tracker hook is effectively not wired in. Result: every compose call hits the try/except at line 265 and returns `{success: false, error: "name 'tt_cfg' is not defined", fallback: true}`. HTTP is still 200 (returned via fallback) but `success` is false and `message` is missing.

minor.issue: Response uses key `message` (capability_response shape) instead of `reply` as described in the spec. Routing works (no 500), content correct, just a key-name mismatch — confirm with main agent whether spec or implementation is canonical.

action_items: FIX response_composer.compose_response(): after computing `turns`, add `from modules.chat.topic_tracker import detect_topic; tt_cfg = bp.get('topic_tracker', {}) or {}; topic = detect_topic(session_id, max_turns=tt_cfg.get('max_turns_lookback', 6)) if (session_id and tt_cfg.get('enabled', True)) else None`. Then pass `topic=topic` into `_build_system_prompt(...)`. This makes the existing line 256 (`'topic': topic if tt_cfg.get('expose_in_meta', True) else None`) valid and actually wires the topic_tracker hook into the pipeline.
Verify `_build_system_prompt` is called with the new `topic` kwarg (current call at line 208 omits it).
Decide whether /api/chat/message should return `reply` or `message` and align spec ↔ implementation.
critical_code_review_comments: Topic tracker integration is half-done: blueprint config present, helper module present, BUT compose_response never imports topic_tracker and never defines tt_cfg/topic — so the feature is fully dead in production despite passing static parse checks.

compose_response try/except at lines 220-266 is too broad: it swallows the NameError silently into a generic fallback response, masking integration bugs. Recommend logging the exception (logger.exception) instead of `pass`-style fallback.

Both `topic` and `tt_cfg` referenced before assignment is a classic NameError that any unit test of compose_response with a mocked LlmChat would have caught — add at least one minimal unit test that covers the happy path of compose_response.
seed_data_creation: Test deletes /app/backend/data/chat/logs/test-fork-topic.json before run to ensure fresh session.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Re-run /app/backend/tests/test_spark_core_v2_topic_tracker.py after main agent fixes compose_response. Expected after fix: all 7 tests pass. Note that the topic value will only appear from turn 3 onwards (min_score_to_inject=2 in blueprint), so the assertion is on the LAST response only — this is correct given 3 sequential calls in the same session with related philosophical terms.
rca of the issue: RCA: During the topic_tracker feature deploy, the developer added topic_tracker.py, added topic_tracker config to response_composer.json, added the `topic` parameter to `_build_system_prompt`, and added `'topic': topic if tt_cfg.get('expose_in_meta', True) else None` to the compose_response return dict — BUT forgot to actually compute `topic` and `tt_cfg` inside compose_response (the variables only exist in _build_system_prompt's scope). The transient IndentationError on line 267 mentioned in the prompt is now gone (the duplicate block was cleaned up), but the underlying integration is still half-applied. Reproduction: POST /api/spark/compose with any text → response is {success:false, error:"name 'tt_cfg' is not defined", fallback:true}. Mitigation: see action_items above — define tt_cfg and topic inside compose_response and pass topic to _build_system_prompt.
